title: squalify must have its own mark as the package icon and README image
lead: Creates a squalify mark in the squalor branding system and uses it as the NuGet package icon for `squalor.squalify` and `squalor.squalify.Cli`, plus the README and docs header images.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
Owner (2026-10-27), verbatim: "no icon for now, land them when they pass.  create a slice for creating an icon/logo/images -- we can tag that to the next release target". v0.1.0 ships without an icon; this slice targets the release after it.

nuget.org's ID prefix reservation criteria ask that packages with an icon use the embedded `icon` element (not `iconUrl`). `branding/` has marks for other squalor tools but none for squalify.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `branding/` (the squalor branding repo): a squalify mark made by that repo's own process (`branding/generated/logos/MARKS.md`, `STYLE_GUIDE.md`), with a 128x128 PNG export for NuGet. That work lands in the branding repo; this slice consumes its export.
- `src/squalify/squalify.csproj` and `src/squalify.Cli/squalify.Cli.csproj` (or `Directory.Build.props` for packable projects): `PackageIcon` with the PNG packed at the package root.
- `README.md`: header image, with an absolute URL so it renders on nuget.org.
- `docs/how-it-works.md` (optional): the mark in the header, re-rendered.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body: 1. `Package_Library_HasEmbeddedIcon`: the packed library and CLI nupkgs contain the icon file, and the nuspec names it in `<icon>`.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. Agree the mark with the owner in the branding repo first.
2. Write the test, watch it fail, add the icon, watch it pass.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
- `dotnet build squalify.sln -c Release`
- `dotnet test squalify.sln -c Release`
- `dotnet format squalify.sln --verify-no-changes`
- `slicer check`

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: Worktree `.worktrees/sq-30` on branch `sq-30`. No agent commits.
